answer: Simulate a 2D lid-driven cavity flow using OpenFOAM icoFoam (incompressible, laminar, no turbulence models). The domain is a 0.1 m x 0.1 m square cavity discretized as a structured hex mesh via blockMesh with 20 cells in X, 20 cells in Y, and 1 cell in Z (thickness 0.01 m), uniform grading (1 1 1), cell size 0.005 m x 0.005 m x 0.01 m. Define patches as follows: top face (y=0.1) named movingWall, left/right/bottom faces named fixedWalls, front/back z-faces named frontAndBack. Set fluid kinematic viscosity nu = 0.001 m^2/s in constant/transportProperties (yielding Re = U*L/nu = 1*0.1/0.001 = 100). Set initial conditions in the 0/ directory: U = (0 0 0) everywhere, p = 0 everywhere. Set boundary conditions for velocity: movingWall gets fixedValue uniform (1 0 0), fixedWalls get fixedValue uniform (0 0 0), frontAndBack gets type empty. Set boundary conditions for pressure: movingWall and fixedWalls get zeroGradient, frontAndBack gets type empty. Do NOT add pRefCell or pRefValue to system/controlDict. In system/controlDict write exactly these six entries: startTime 0, stopAt endTime, endTime 0.5, deltaT 0.002, writeControl timeStep, writeInterval 20. No adjustTimeStep, no maxCo, no adaptive stepping. Create system/fvSchemes and system/fvSolution by copying verbatim from the official OpenFOAM tutorial incompressible/icoFoam/cavity/cavity/system/ for the target OpenFOAM version (do not invent or modify entries). The PISO block inside fvSolution includes pRefCell 0 and pRefValue 0 as part of the tutorial solver settings; this is distinct from controlDict and is permitted. Do not create an fvConstraints file. Run the solver icoFoam to produce results up to t = 0.5 s (250 time steps, 12 intermediate write folders plus the final one). No post-processing beyond the native icoFoam output.
